_note: English names and rule summaries used when the interface is in English. The English names come from BSData/mordheim (keys of fr.json); only names that need fixing are listed in 'guerriers', 'competences' and 'equipement'. Rule summaries are written for the app (no text copied from the books).

Leader.resume: Warriors of the warband within 6" of the leader may use his Leadership for their Leadership tests.

Reikland Leadership.resume: Trained in military discipline, warriors may use their captain's Leadership within 12" instead of 6". Marksmen, the famous Reikland archers, have +1 BS (already included in their profile).

Middenheim Strength.resume: Northerners are built like oxen: the captain and champions start with Strength 4 instead of 3 (already included in their profile).

Great Traders.resume: Thanks to their guild contacts, Marienburgers add +1 to their rolls to find rare items. Their wealth gives them 600 gc at the start of a campaign instead of 500 (+20% in a one-off game).

Mutations.resume: The model may start with one or more mutations, bought when recruited. A Mutant must have at least one.

Fear.resume: Causes fear: an enemy charged by this model, or wishing to charge it, must first pass a Leadership test. Creatures that cause fear are not afraid of others that cause fear.

Crazed.resume: Driven mad by daemonic possession, Darksouls know no fear and automatically pass all their Leadership tests.

Fanatic.resume: Carried by their faith, Flagellants automatically pass all their Leadership tests but can never become the warband's leader.

Burn The Witch.resume: The Witch Hunter fiercely hates all spellcasters (see Hatred).

Hatred.resume: In the first turn of each close combat against a hated enemy, the model may re-roll all its missed to hit rolls.

Blessed Sight.resume: The Augur may re-roll failed characteristic tests and failed to hit rolls (shooting and close combat); the second result stands. If she was not taken out of action, roll two dice for her in the exploration phase and keep the one you prefer.

Immune To Psycology.resume: Never affected by psychology (fear, rout…) and never leaves a close combat of its own accord.

Imune to Poison.resume: Poisons have no effect on this model.

No Pain.resume: A Stunned result is treated as Knocked Down.

May not run.resume: Cannot run, but may charge normally.

No Brain.resume: A mindless creature: never gains experience.

Charge.resume: Dire Wolves have 2 Attacks instead of 1 in the turn they charge.

Stupidity.resume: At the start of each of its turns the model tests its Leadership. If it fails, it casts no spells and does not fight until its next turn; outside close combat it moves randomly or stays still.

Large Target.resume: Large target: shooters get +1 to hit it and may target it even if it is not the closest enemy.

Wizard (Chaos Rituals).resume: Casts spells from the Chaos Rituals.

Wizard (Magic of the Horned Rat).resume: Casts spells from the Magic of the Horned Rat.

Prayers of Sigmar.resume: May use the Prayers of Sigmar the way a wizard casts spells.

Always Hungry.resume: The Troll costs 15 gc upkeep after each game. Failing that, the Boss may sacrifice two Goblins or Squigs to it; otherwise the Troll wanders off in search of food.

Ancient Enemies.resume: A Kislevite warband can never ally with a Chaos warband (Possessed, Beastmen, Skaven, Dark Elves, Chaos Dwarfs…).

Animal.resume: The Minotaur may gain experience but never becomes a Hero.

Animosity.resume: At the start of the turn, roll a D6 for each Orc or Goblin Henchman not in close combat. On a 1 it squabbles: depending on a second roll it may charge or shoot a nearby Orc or Goblin, stay put, or rush towards the enemy.

Armour Use.resume: Dwarfs never suffer a movement penalty for wearing armour.

Bear Handler.resume: Allows the warband to recruit a Trained Bear. Within 6" of its tamer (even if knocked down or stunned) the bear automatically passes its Stupidity tests.

Bear Hug.resume: If the bear hits the same target with both its attacks, it may replace them with a hug: each rolls a D6 + Strength; if the bear equals or beats its opponent, the victim suffers a wound with no armour save.

Bloodgreed.resume: If the Minotaur takes all its close combat opponents out of action, it becomes frenzied on a 4+.

Cloud of Flies.resume: The flies around it pester its opponents: -1 to hit it in close combat.

Daemonic.resume: A daemon made of the unchanging stuff of Chaos rather than flesh: never gains experience.

Demonic.resume: A daemon made of the unchanging stuff of Chaos rather than flesh: never gains experience.

Daemonic Aura.resume: 5+ special save, modified by the Strength of the attack and negated by magic weapons and spells. Its attacks count as magical.

Daemonic Instability.resume: When taken out of action it is banished on a 1-3 (no serious injury roll). If the warband routs, each must pass a Leadership test or be destroyed.

Dangerous to Know.resume: Too pestilent for any mercenary to survive: the Carnival may not hire any Hired Swords.

Deathwish.resume: The Slayer seeks a glorious death: immune to psychology, he never has to test when fighting alone.

Distasteful Company.resume: Few mercenaries will serve Orcs: only Pit Fighters, Ogre Bodyguards and Warlocks may be hired.

Drunk.resume: Soaked in rotgut, Ruffians automatically pass all their Leadership tests.

Drunken.resume: At the start of each turn roll a D6: on a 1 the Centigor is subject to Stupidity, on a 6 to Frenzy. While under either, it ignores all other psychology.

Dumb Monster.resume: Too dim to learn: the Troll never gains experience.

Expert Weaponsmith.resume: While the Engineer stays in the warband, the range of Dwarf missile weapons increases by 3" for pistols and by 6" for crossbows and handguns.

Fiercely Loyal.resume: As long as his bear is not taken out of action, the tamer treats the Sold to the Pits, Robbed and Captured serious injury results as Full Recovery.

Goblin Animosity.resume: A Goblin rolling 'I heard that!' never dares charge an Orc; it may still shoot at one.

Grudgebearers.resume: Remembering ancient wars, a Dwarf warband never hires Hired Swords or Dramatis Personae who are Elves.

Guardian.resume: The Guardian is one with the cart: he never leaves it, is only harmed if the cart is destroyed, gains no experience, and his attacks pass on Nurgle's Rot.

Gun-Rest.resume: Armed with a halberd and a handgun, a Streltsi who does not move may rest his gun on the halberd: +1 to hit with the handgun.

Hard Head.resume: Dwarfs ignore the special rules of maces, clubs and other bludgeoning weapons used against them.

Hard to Kill.resume: On the injury chart, 1-2 = knocked down, 3-5 = stunned, 6 = out of action.

Hate Chaos.resume: Cossacks hate all Chaos forces (see Hatred).

Hate Orcs and Goblins.resume: All Dwarfs hate Orcs and Goblins (see Hatred).

Immune to Poison.resume: Poisons have no effect on this model.

Immune to Psychology.resume: Never affected by psychology (fear, rout…) and never leaves a close combat of its own accord.

Incomparable Miners.resume: Experts in ores, Dwarfs add +1 to the number of wyrdstone shards found at the end of each game.

Lowest of the Low.resume: At the bottom of the pecking order, an Ungor never becomes a Hero: re-roll the 'That lad's got talent' result.

May Hire.resume: A Kislevite warband may hire the same Hired Swords as human mercenary warbands.

Minderz.resume: Each Squig must stay within 6" of a Goblin. Otherwise, at the start of its move it goes wild and bounces 2D6" in a random direction until the end of the game.

Movement.resume: The Squig has no fixed Movement: it bounces 2D6", never runs and does not declare charges, but counts as charging if it moves into contact with an enemy.

No Respect.resume: Pitied and feared, Ruffians can never become the warband's leader.

Not Orcs.resume: For the rout test, each Goblin or Squig out of action counts as only half a model.

Nurgle’s Blessings.resume: A Tainted One starts the game with at least one Blessing of Nurgle, bought when recruited.

Nurgle’s Rot.resume: Immune to poison. On a to hit roll of 6 in close combat, a living target catches the Rot: before each game it must pass a Toughness test or permanently lose 1 point of Toughness.

Plague Cart.resume: The cart raises the warband's maximum size by 2. Plague Bearers and Nurglings re-roll their instability tests and add +1 to their wound rolls.

Prayers of Taal.resume: May use the Prayers of Taal the way a wizard casts spells.

Promotion.resume: A Halfling promoted to Hero ('That lad's got talent') may not choose the Strength skill list.

Regeneration.resume: Each wound inflicted on the Troll is ignored on a 4+, unless caused by fire or fire magic. The Troll never rolls for serious injuries after the game.

Runts.resume: A Goblin rolling 'That lad's got talent' is promptly killed by his Orc masters: remove him from the roster.

Self Sufficient.resume: Ostlanders don't pay outsiders: they hire no Hired Swords except Ogres.

Set Traps.resume: By spending a turn doing nothing else, the Bergjaeger places a trap counter. Any model moving within 2" sets it off on a 3+ and suffers a Strength 4 hit; the counter is then removed.

Slow Witted.resume: The Ogre needs twice as much experience as the others for each advance.

Stream of Corruption.resume: Shooting attack with a 6" range, Strength 3, no armour save.

Strictures.resume: A Priest of Taal may never wear heavy armour.

Swarm.resume: A group of Nurglings is not limited to five models.

Trained.resume: Subject to Stupidity unless within 6" of the Bear Tamer, whose Leadership it alone may use. The bear does not take part if the tamer is missing.

Trample.resume: The Centigor's hooves give it an extra attack that gets no weapon bonus or penalty.

Unnatural Strength.resume: Brutes start with the Strongman skill.

Vomit Attack.resume: Instead of its normal attacks, the Troll may vomit on an opponent in base contact: a single attack that hits automatically at Strength 5, with no armour save.

Woodland Dwelling.resume: The Centigor suffers no movement penalty in woods.

Wizard (Nurgle Rituals).resume: Casts spells from the Nurgle Rituals.

Strike To Injure.resume: Adds +1 to injury rolls in close combat.

Combat Master.resume: When fighting more than one enemy, the warrior gets +1 Attack, and he is immune to the 'All Alone' rule.

Weapons Traning.resume: May use any close combat weapon, not only those in his equipment list.

Web Of Steel.resume: Adds +1 to the roll for critical hits in close combat.

Expert Swordsman.resume: When charging with a sword, may re-roll all missed attacks in that turn.

Step Aside.resume: Special 5+ save against each wound suffered in close combat, not modified by the attacker's Strength.

Quick Shot.resume: May shoot twice per turn with a bow or crossbow (not a crossbow pistol).

Pistolier.resume: With a brace of pistols of any type, may fire twice in the shooting phase (reloading still applies).

Eagle Eyes.resume: Adds +6" to the range of his missile weapons.

Weapons Expert.resume: May use any missile weapon, not only those in his equipment list.

Nimble.resume: May move and fire with weapons that normally cannot be fired after moving. Cannot be combined with Quick Shot.

Trick Shooter.resume: Ignores all cover modifiers when shooting.

Hunter.resume: Reloads so fast that he may fire a handgun or Hochland long rifle every turn.

Knife Fighter.resume: May throw up to three throwing knives or stars in the shooting phase, split between targets as he wishes.

Battle Tongue.resume: Leader only: warriors within 12" instead of 6" may use his Leadership.

Sorcery.resume: Wizards only: +1 to rolls to cast spells.

Streetwise.resume: Adds +2 to rarity rolls when looking for rare items.

Haggle.resume: After each game, reduces the price of one item by 2D6 gc (to a minimum of 1 gc).

Arcane Lore.resume: With a Tome of Magic, the warrior may learn Lesser Magic. Not available to Witch Hunters, Sisters of Sigmar or Warrior Priests.

Wyrdstone Hunter.resume: If the Hero searches the ruins in the exploration phase, you may re-roll one dice when finding wyrdstone.

Warrior Wizard.resume: Wizards only: may cast spells while wearing armour.

Mighty Blow.resume: +1 Strength in close combat (not with pistols).

Pit Fighter.resume: +1 Weapon Skill and +1 Attack when fighting inside buildings or ruins.

Resilient.resume: Hits against him in close combat suffer -1 Strength (armour save modifiers are unchanged).

Strongman.resume: May use a double-handed weapon without striking last.

Leap.resume: May leap D6" in the movement phase on top of his normal move, over models, obstacles and gaps.

Sprint.resume: Triples his Movement when running or charging instead of doubling it.

Acrobat.resume: Can jump down from up to 12" without harm with a single Initiative test, and may re-roll failed diving charges.

Lightning Reflexes.resume: When charged, he strikes first against the models that charged him.

Jump Up.resume: Ignores Knocked Down results on the injury chart, unless caused by a helmet save or the No Pain rule.

Dodge.resume: Special 5+ save against each hit from missile weapons, taken before rolling to wound.

Scale Sheer Surfaces.resume: May climb up to twice his Movement and never needs to test for climbing.

Severe Arm Wound.resume: Roll a D6: on a 1 the arm is lost and the warrior may only use a single one-handed weapon from now on; on a 2-6 he misses the next game.

Madness: Stupidity.resume: The warrior is subject to Stupidity from now on.

Madness: Frenzy.resume: The warrior is subject to Frenzy from now on.

Chest Wound.resume: -1 Toughness, and the warrior misses the next game.

Blind In one Eye.resume: -1 Ballistic Skill. A warrior blinded in both eyes must retire.

Old Battle Wound.resume: Before each game, roll a D6: on a 1 the warrior cannot take part.

Bitter Emity.resume: The warrior hates the model or warband that injured him (see Hatred).

Hardened.resume: The warrior is immune to fear.

Smashed Leg.resume: Roll a D6: on a 1 the warrior may no longer run (he may still charge); on a 2-6 he misses the next game.

Black Hunger.resume: Declared at the start of the Skaven Hero's turn: +1 Attack and +D3" Movement for that turn, but he suffers D3 Strength 3 hits with no armour save at the end of the turn.

Tail Fighting.resume: The Skaven wields a shield, a knife or a sword with its tail: +1 Attack with that weapon, or +1 to its armour save.

Wall Runner.resume: The Skaven never needs to take Initiative tests when climbing walls and other sheer surfaces.

Infiltration.resume: Deployed after the enemy warband, anywhere on the table out of sight of the enemy and more than 12" from any enemy model. If both sides infiltrate, each rolls a D6 and the lowest sets up first.

Art of Silent Death.resume: Fights unarmed without penalty and counts as having two weapons (+1 Attack). Causes a critical hit on a to wound roll of 5-6. With Eshin Fighting Claws, +2 Attacks instead of +1.

Horned One.resume: Mighty horns give the Beastman an extra Attack at his basic Strength in the turn he charges.

Sign of Sigmar.resume: Possessed and Undead opponents lose their first attack against her in the first round of close combat (to a minimum of 1).

Protection of Sigmar.resume: Any spell that would affect her is cancelled on a D6 roll of 4+; a cancelled spell affects no other model either.

Utter Determination.resume: Matriarch only: she may re-roll any failed Rout test.

Righteous Fury.resume: Hates all Skaven, Undead and Possessed warbands and every model in them.

Absolute Faith.resume: May re-roll all Fear tests and never has to test when fighting alone against several enemies.

Extra Tough.resume: Re-roll the serious injury roll when this Hero is taken out of action.

Resource Hunter.resume: When rolling on the Exploration chart, the Hero may modify one dice by +1 or -1.

True Grit.resume: On the injury chart, 1-3 = knocked down, 4-5 = stunned, 6 = out of action.

Thick Skull.resume: 3+ save on a D6 to avoid being stunned (2+ with a helmet): a saved stunned result becomes knocked down.

Waaagh!.resume: May add +D3" to his charge range.

Ferocious Charge.resume: May double his Attacks in the turn he charges, at -1 to hit that turn.

Monster Slayer.resume: Always wounds on a 4+ whatever the target's Toughness, unless his own Strength (with weapon modifiers) would wound on a lower roll.

Berserker.resume: +1 to hit in the turn he charges.

Frenzy.resume: Must charge the nearest enemy within range and doubles its Attacks in close combat. Immune to psychology unless knocked down or stunned.
